settings.label: WhatsApp number
settings.info: With country code, digits only (e.g. 971501234567). Used by the WhatsApp float and concierge.

settings.content: The free-delivery threshold was hard-coded in eighteen files — the cart bar, the trust strips, the FAQs, the announcement bar — and changing it meant finding all of them. It is one number now. It must match the shipping rate in Shopify admin › Settings › Shipping and delivery, and the Shipping policy text, neither of which the theme can set.

settings.label: Free delivery above
settings.info: Digits only, in store currency. Orders at or above this total ship free.

settings.label: Return window (days)
settings.info: Digits only. Must match Settings › Policies › Refund policy. The storefront also states what returns are accepted for — faulty, wrong or incomplete orders — because a bare number reads as a change-of-mind window, which this store does not offer.

settings.content: "Delivered by Thursday" answers the question "ships in 1–4 business days" leaves open, and 20% of shoppers who abandon a checkout say delivery was too slow — a figure they can only act on if they are told before the payment step. The dates below are worked out from these three numbers and the UAE working week (Monday–Friday), and they must match the Shipping policy and the courier's real service, which the theme cannot see.

settings.label: Same-day dispatch cutoff
settings.info: Store time, 24-hour. Orders placed after this hour start their clock the next business day.

settings.label: Slowest delivery
settings.info: Business days after dispatch. Shown as the "by" date, so this is the promise — keep it the one the courier actually meets.

settings.content: Funnel tracking. Every CRO decision after this depends on seeing where shoppers drop off, so this is the one thing to fill in first. Paste a GA4 measurement ID, a GTM container ID, or both — leave both blank and nothing loads at all, which is the right default for a theme preview or a staging copy. The theme pushes the full GA4 ecommerce event set to window.dataLayer either way, so a GTM container can read the same events without a measurement ID here.

settings.label: GA4 measurement ID
settings.info: Starts G-. Loads gtag.js and sends events straight to GA4. Leave blank if a GTM container below is sending them instead — filling in both sends every event twice.

settings.label: Google Tag Manager container ID
settings.info: Starts GTM-. Loads the container, which then reads the dataLayer the theme writes.

settings.content: A theme cannot see the checkout, so begin_checkout is the last event this file can fire. purchase, add_shipping_info and add_payment_info have to come from a custom pixel in Settings › Customer events — the code to paste is in docs/ga4-purchase-pixel.js. Without it the funnel ends at the checkout button and conversion rate cannot be calculated.

settings.label: Log events to the browser console
settings.info: For checking a release. Leave off in production.

settings.content: A theme cannot store a rating. The storefront has no database and cannot write to Shopify — only the Admin API can put a value on an order, and an Admin token in theme code would expose the whole shop. So Judge.me keeps the ratings and sends the request; the theme only asks. Paste the Judge.me shop-review form link below and a "How was your experience?" card appears on a customer's order once that order is fulfilled. Leave it blank and nothing renders, rather than five stars that lead nowhere. Find the link in Judge.me › Shop reviews. Judge.me also sends its own request automatically after fulfilment — set the timing there, not here, and give the courier time to actually arrive before it goes out.

settings.label: Judge.me shop review form link
settings.info: Full URL, starting https://. The chosen star is appended as &rating=1–5; if Judge.me ignores it the form simply opens unset.

settings.content: The first-order discount shown above the footer. A theme cannot create a discount, so the code below must exist in Shopify admin › Discounts: a discount code, percentage off the order, customer eligibility set to customers with an account, and "limit to one use per customer" ticked. The theme puts the code on the bag; Shopify decides who may keep it.

settings.label: Discount code
settings.info: Must match the code in Shopify admin › Discounts exactly. Case does not matter.

settings.label: Percentage shown in the copy
settings.info: Digits only. This is wording, not the discount itself — change the real amount on the discount in admin and keep the two in step.

settings.label: Minimum order value
settings.info: Digits only, in store currency. Must match the discount's minimum purchase amount in admin, or the storefront promises a discount that checkout refuses. Leave blank if the discount has no minimum.
